.

 
Brief Hospital Course:
1)Abdominal pain  
Although presentation is similar to previous episode of 
pancreatitis, during this episode patient's lipase was not 
elevated.  CT findings were only mildly suggestive of 
pancreatitis, and location of patient's pain and tenderness to 
the right side of the abdomen does not match area of 
inflammation seen on CT.  Recent biopsies showed chronic 
duodenitis, raising small bowel disease as an etiology.  Patient 
underwent and EGD and capsule endoscopy with biopsies.  The 
gross appearance on endoscopy was not revealing of an etiology.  
Given prior history of inflammation on sigmoidoscopy, this could 
represent a manifestation of IBD.  At time of discharge etiology 
of pain remained unclear.
  Therapeutically, patient was initially maintained NPO with IV 
fluids, IV narcotics, and anti-emetics. She made slow progress 
to clear liquids, and then was able to take toast.  Once she was 
taking clears she was switched successfully to oral dilaudid.  
At time of discharge she tolerated clear liquids and toast and 
was able to stay adequately hydrated.  Her exam began to improve 
and she had minimal tenderness in the epigastrium and RUQ.
  A colonoscopy was planned, however after ___'s prep patient 
still had residual stool in the colon.  After first attempted 
colonoscopy patient had multiple bowel movements and reported 
passing clear stool.  Unfortunately on repeat colonoscopy later 
that afternoon she still had significant stool present.  GI felt 
she would need to return for colonoscopy with 2 days of GoLytely 
prep.
.  
2)UTI:  
Treated for a total of 3 days with levofloxacin for UTI 
diagnosed at ___.
.

Patient did not feel symptomatic either in terms of

active she would become more tachycardic and betaxolol was 
continued on discharge.
.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted for abdominal pain.  This was treated with 
bowel rest, and improved over the course of days.  You also had 
an upper endoscopy and to help evaluate the source of your pain. 
 You will need to have the lower endoscopy in the future to 
further evaluate your colon.  Next time, you will need to take 
Golytely prep over 2 days to ensure that the colon is clean.

Since you are now more able to take in clear liquids and toast, 
it is safe for you to return home.  You should continue to 
advance your diet judiciously.  If you are unable to tolerate 
clear liquids, please return to the emergency room.  Please also 
seek medical attention if you experience lightheadedness, 
worsening abdominal pain, shortness of breath, or any other new 
or concerning symptoms.
